args.title: Reject invalid TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES values to prevent misinterpretation
args.body:
File: src/config.ts

Add validation to reject non-integer or non-minute formatted TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES environment variables to prevent the service from silently accepting invalid values like '12h' and interpreting them incorrectly as 12 minutes.

label: bug
file: src/config.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

The environment variable TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES is read as an integer number of minutes. A setting like '12h' is silently accepted but treated as 12, causing the token lifetime to be only 12 minutes. The fix is to add validation rejecting non-integer values and to document the expected unit as minutes.

label: question
file: none
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

The health check endpoint returns status 200 with a detailed JSON status that can be "degraded". The question is whether this status should be treated as healthy for load balancer probes or cause removal from rotation. The API currently uses the HTTP status to indicate critical failure only.

label: docs
file: docs/API.md
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

The issue requests documentation of the password validation rules for the reset API, as currently users get 'validation failed' errors with no indication why. The API docs should specify the password requirements (e.g., minimum length) so help desk staff can assist users appropriately.

args.title: Fix Accept-Language header parsing to respect 'q' values for locale selection
args.body:
File: src/i18n/index.ts

Improve the pickLocale function to parse the Accept-Language header and respect the quality (q) values to select the best supported locale, instead of picking the first supported language in the list. This fixes responses coming back in English when French has a higher q value.

label: bug
file: src/i18n/index.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

The pickLocale function currently selects the first supported language in the Accept-Language header, ignoring the quality values (q). This causes incorrect locale selection when the client prefers a language with a higher q value later in the list. The fix is to parse and respect q values to pick the best supported locale.
